title: Cohort-based image deprecation policy and compatibility assertions for LTS channels
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement a cohort-based deprecation and compatibility-assertion workflow for container images and driver stacks that are published to our LTS and stable channels. Goals: reduce surprise regressions during runtime upgrades, provide deterministic rollback gates, and maintain a searchable, versioned SBOM index tied to image cohorts. This ticket covers policy, tooling (indexer + attestations), rollout gates, monitoring dashboards, and an emergency rollback playbook.
acceptance_criteria: Policy doc accepted by Release and Security teams and linked from the Release playbook
Automated SBOM indexer produces per-image assertions (artifact SHA -> list of validated drivers/kernels) for all images in stable/LTS channels
Cohort assignment service can mark images into canary/stage/stable cohorts and expose cohort metadata via API
Rollout gate integration with canary cohorts enforces compatibility assertions before promoting an image to the next cohort
Dashboard shows cohort promotion history, failure reasons, and token-level cost delta for promoted images
Rollback playbook tested in staging with a simulated driver mismatch and documented in Confluence
comments: 2025-02-14 Aisha: Initial ticket created after postmortem (INC-2025-01) showed two customer regressions from an unpinned CUDA library in a stable image. Proposed cohort model (canary=5% hosts, stage=25%, stable=remaining) and SBOM-index assertions.

2025-02-18 Marco: Spike results uploaded to GH - added prototype indexer that extracts SBOM and probes driver compatibility matrix using existing driver-prober (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4213). Early results: 98% of images map cleanly to compatible driver sets; 2% need rebuilds or explicit driver pins.

2025-02-20 Security review: Requested explicit signing of compatibility assertions and audit trail retention for 180 days. See Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/REL/Cohort+Deprecation+Policy

2025-02-25 Design review (Kenji): Suggested UI flags in Console rollout flow to display cohort and failing assertion reasons (missing DLLs, kernel mismatch, quantization ABI mismatch). Added label requirements for artifacts.

2025-02-27 Eng update: Implemented cohort metadata endpoint (/v1/internal/artifacts/{sha}/cohorts) and added a migration to populate cohorts for the last 90 days of images. Unit tests passing; integration tests failing on a timing issue in the promotion worker (investigating).

2025-02-28 Marco: Integration test failure root cause: worker retries overlapped causing double-promotions. Mitigation: add a DB advisory lock and idempotency token. Patch in review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/release-orch/pull/88

2025-03-02 Ops: Canary promotion dry-run executed against cluster-staging; observed a 0.6% latency tail increase for one model shard due to a new kernel selection; Decision: block automatic stable promotion until kernel selection fallback is implemented. Logged as blocker for stable promotion.

2025-03-03 Aisha: Updated acceptance criteria to include 'compatibility assertion signing' per security feedback and set security_review_required=true. Next steps: complete promotion-worker fix, add attestation signer, and schedule a tabletop rollback drill.
